title: A chatbot predicts, it doesn't look up
summary: Large language models are trained to predict the next token of text. Chained thousands of times, that produces fluent answers — which is also why they can be confidently wrong.
evidenceNote: A simplified picture. Modern assistants are also tuned with human feedback and may use tools such as web search, but next-token prediction is the core mechanism.

scenes.text: A chatbot doesn't look up answers. It predicts them.
Large language models are trained on huge amounts of text to predict the next small chunk of text — a 'token'.

scenes.answer: "Stockholm" is by far the most likely next token — so the model writes it.

scenes.text: Repeat that step thousands of times and you get an essay.

items.title: Probabilities
items.detail: Each next token is picked from likely options

items.title: Training
items.detail: Billions of examples tune the model's parameters

scenes.text: This is also why chatbots can be confidently wrong.
scenes.reveal: A fluent, plausible answer isn't the same as a checked fact.

scenes.text: Use AI to think and draft. Verify anything that matters.
